name: Use of Color
explanation: This criterion says color cannot be the only way you convey information, indicate an action, prompt a response, or distinguish one visual element from another. If sighted users need to notice a difference in color to understand something, there must also be a non-color cue: text, an icon, an underline, a pattern, or a change in shape. This doesn't mean you can't use color — it means color can't be doing the job alone. A classic failure is a form that marks required fields only by coloring the label red, or a line chart that distinguishes data series only by hue with no labels. A classic pass is the same form using a red label plus the word 'required,' or the same chart using distinct line styles in addition to color.
whoItAffects: People who are colorblind may not be able to distinguish red from green at all — red-green colorblindness affects roughly 1 in 12 men. A red border that looks obviously different to someone with typical color vision can be invisible as a distinct signal to them. People with low vision using high contrast mode or a customized color scheme may have colors overridden or muted entirely. Users on grayscale or e-ink displays, or printing a page in black and white, lose all color information. Blind users relying on a screen reader get no color information at all unless it's also expressed in text, so 'the red asterisk means required' communicates nothing unless the word 'required' is actually present.

codeExample.bad: Enter a valid email address
codeExample.good: ⚠ Error: Enter a valid email address

howToTest: Set your operating system or browser to grayscale and browse the page. For every place color is used to convey a status, a required field, a link, or an error, check whether you can still tell what it means with the color removed. It fails this criterion if a red-bordered field, a colored-only link in body text, or a chart legend becomes ambiguous or indistinguishable in grayscale.

check.question: A signup form marks required fields by making the field label text red, with no other indicator. Which statement is correct?
choices: This fails SC 1.4.1 because color is the only way required fields are indicated
This passes SC 1.4.1 because red is a strong, high-contrast color
This fails SC 1.4.3 (Contrast) instead of SC 1.4.1, since it's about color choice
This passes as long as the red meets the minimum contrast ratio
